title: X is finally getting its first parental controls
summary: X is finally rolling out parental controls that allow parents and guardians to manage teens' accounts on the platform. content: X is finally rolling out parental controls that allow parents and guardians to manage teens' accounts on the platform. While teens will retain ownership of their own account, parents and guardians will be able to see how much time their child has spent on X, set daily limits, require approval for new followers, and limit For You recommendations to accounts a teen already follows. "Parents and guardians cannot read private messages, see searches or viewing history, post as their teen, or access the account," explains the X safety team. content: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts - more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors - with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold." In October, Character.AI filed for bankruptcy following years of scandals and legal challenges , including from Disney . content: A couple of Walmart's budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google's familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required to access the feature. Both cameras and Google's Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd gen) also have a new remote control in the Google Home app you can use to start or stop a 30-second security siren while watching the camera's live video feed. content: Most people know not to try to pass highway patrol cars while performing a traffic break on a freeway. But on November 6th, a driverless Waymo on Interstate 280 failed that test. Video shows the robotaxi attempting to overtake two California Highway Patrol cruisers during a traffic break, a moving violation that could get a human driver's license suspended.
